This folder documents the current project idea and the working system flow for the
Jarvis Assistant so far.

## One-Line Idea

Jarvis is an emotion-aware voice assistant that accepts text or speech, detects the
user's emotional state, retrieves persona-aware response guidance, stores recent
conversation context, and returns both a text reply and a synthesized voice artifact.

## Current Product Shape

- Frontend: browser console at `/ui` with text chat, manual voice turns, wake phrase
  support, wellness demo inputs, emotion monitor, conversation history, and audio
  playback.
- Backend: FastAPI service with REST endpoints for chat, voice upload, history, and
  health checks.
- Orchestration: `AssistantOrchestrator` coordinates transcription, emotion detection,
  memory, LLM response generation, and text-to-speech output.
- Persona guidance: `app/services/rag.py` loads a prebuilt
  `persona_id + detected_emotion` cache from `corpus/persona_guidance.json` before
  prompt rendering, avoiding runtime vector search or extra LLM calls.
- Memory: recent turns are stored as `ConversationTurn` rows with role, content,
  session id, emotion, and timestamp.
- Database: MySQL is the primary configured database; SQLite is used as a fallback
  when MySQL is unavailable.

## Models And Providers In Use

The current `.env` is configured for the legacy voice pipeline and Bedrock LLM path.
Secrets are intentionally not documented here.

| Layer | Active / Configured Model | Provider / Library | Current Status | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Main LLM | `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0` | AWS Bedrock | Active because `LLM_PROVIDER=bedrock` | Generates Jarvis responses using prompt context, detected emotion, wellness signal, and recent history. |
| Alternate LLM | `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` | Groq | Configured as an alternate, inactive unless `LLM_PROVIDER=groq` | Can replace Bedrock for chat completion generation. |
| Realtime Model | `gpt-4o-mini-realtime-preview` | OpenAI config value | Configured but not wired into the current FastAPI flow | Reserved for possible future realtime voice work. |
| Speech-to-Text | `base` | OpenAI Whisper package | Active in legacy voice mode | Transcribes uploaded voice audio into text. |
| Audio Emotion | `Dpngtm/wav2vec2-emotion-recognition` | Hugging Face Transformers | Active in legacy voice mode when dependencies are available | Classifies the audio emotion from the uploaded clip. |
| Text Emotion | Keyword scoring map in `EmotionService` | Local Python logic | Active for text chat and hybrid voice emotion decisions | Detects emotion cues from transcript text. |
| Optional Voice Understanding | `iic/SenseVoiceSmall` | FunASR / ModelScope | Present but disabled because `VOICE_UNDERSTANDING_PROVIDER=legacy` | If enabled, produces transcript, emotion tags, language, and audio event metadata in one pass. |
| Voice Output | `tts_models/en/ljspeech/tacotron2-DDC` | Coqui TTS | Used when installed; otherwise falls back to text artifact output | Synthesizes Jarvis replies into `.wav` files. |

Current generation settings:

- `LLM_TEMPERATURE=0.4`
- `LLM_MAX_TOKENS=300`
- `BEDROCK_REGION=us-west-2`
- `WHISPER_LANGUAGE=en`
- `WHISPER_TASK=transcribe`
- `SENSEVOICE_DEVICE=cpu`
- `SENSEVOICE_LANGUAGE=auto`
- `SENSEVOICE_VAD_MODEL=fsmn-vad`

## Emotion Set

Jarvis uses emotions in three places: detection, LLM tone guidance, and frontend
visual state.

| Emotion | How It Can Be Detected | LLM Response Guidance | UI Treatment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `neutral` | Fallback state, neutral audio, no text keyword hit, SenseVoice `neutral` or `emo_unk` | Concise, helpful, emotionally steady | Neutral baseline |
| `calm` | Audio model label | Relaxed, confident, smooth pacing | Calm visual state |
| `happy` | Audio labels like joy/happiness/happy, positive text keywords, SenseVoice `happy` | Upbeat, clear, positive, still concise | Happy visual state |
| `excited` | Possible audio label or frontend state; text word `excited` currently maps into `happy` | Upbeat and clear when passed through as detected emotion | Excited visual state |
| `surprised` | Audio labels surprise/surprised, SenseVoice `surprised` | Upbeat and clear | Surprised visual state |
| `sad` | Audio labels sad/sadness, sad text keywords, SenseVoice `sad` | Warm, gentle, validating, with a small practical action | Sad visual state |
| `fear` | Audio labels fear/fearful, stress/anxiety text keywords, SenseVoice `fearful` or `fear` | Grounded, reassuring, lower energy, one or two stabilizing next steps | Labeled as stressed/anxious |
| `angry` | Audio labels anger/angry, angry text keywords, SenseVoice `angry` | Calm, de-escalating, respectful, solution-oriented | Angry visual state |
| `disgust` | SenseVoice `disgusted` tag | Falls back to the default LLM guidance unless specific guidance is added | Currently falls back to neutral UI styling |

### Text Emotion Keywords

The local keyword detector currently checks these emotion groups:

- `happy`: happy, excited, great, awesome, good, glad, love, amazing, fantastic, wonderful
- `sad`: sad, upset, frustrated, depressed, down, tired, hurt, cry, lonely, hopeless
- `angry`: angry, mad, furious, annoyed, irritated, hate
- `fear`: afraid, scared, nervous, worried, anxious, panic, overwhelmed, stressed, stress, tense

### Hybrid Emotion Decision Rules

In legacy voice mode, Jarvis combines audio emotion and transcript keyword emotion:

1. Start with the audio classifier result.
2. If no text emotion is found, keep audio emotion or fall back to `neutral`.
3. If audio confidence is below `0.55`, use the text emotion.
4. If audio is `neutral` or `calm` and text confidence is at least `0.45`, use the
   text emotion.
5. If audio and text disagree, use text only when text confidence is at least
   `0.12` higher than audio confidence.
6. Otherwise keep the audio emotion.

## Main Working Flow

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    A[User opens browser UI at /ui] --> B{Interaction type}

    B -->|Text turn| C[POST /api/chat]
    B -->|Voice turn| D[Record audio in browser]
    D --> E[POST /api/voice multipart upload]
    E --> F[Save audio file to uploads/]
    F --> G{VOICE_UNDERSTANDING_PROVIDER}

    G -->|legacy - current config| H[Whisper transcribes audio]
    H --> I[Hybrid emotion detection]
    I --> I1[Audio classifier]
    I --> I2[Transcript keyword scoring]
    I1 --> J[Choose final detected_emotion]
    I2 --> J

    G -->|sensevoice - optional| K[SenseVoice processes audio]
    K --> L[Transcript + emotion + language + event metadata]
    L --> M[Build emotion debug payload]
    J --> N[Handle as chat turn]
    M --> N
    C --> N

    N --> O[Load recent session history]
    O --> P[Retrieve persona + emotion guidance]
    P --> P1[Build prompt context payload]
    P1 --> Q[LLM generates Jarvis reply]
    Q --> R[Coqui TTS attempts voice synthesis]
    R --> S{TTS available?}
    S -->|yes| T[Save generated_audio/session-response.wav]
    S -->|no| U[Save generated_audio/session-response.txt]
    T --> V[Store user and assistant turns in database]
    U --> V
    V --> W[Return ChatResponse JSON]
    W --> X[UI updates transcript, reply, emotion monitor, history, and audio player]
```

## Text Chat Flow

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    A[User sends text] --> B[POST /api/chat]
    B --> C[Detect emotion from text keywords]
    C --> D[Fetch up to 12 recent turns]
    D --> D1[Retrieve persona guidance]
    D1 --> E[Create context payload]
    E --> F[Render prompts/jarvis_chat.txt]
    F --> G{LLM_PROVIDER}
    G -->|bedrock - current| H[Invoke AWS Bedrock model]
    G -->|groq - optional| I[Invoke Groq chat completion]
    H --> J[Jarvis text reply]
    I --> J
    J --> K[Generate TTS or text artifact]
    K --> L[Save user and assistant turns]
    L --> M[Return response to UI]
```

## Emotion Decision Flow

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    A[Transcript and optional audio clip] --> B{Voice path?}
    B -->|Text-only chat| C[Keyword emotion detector]
    C --> D{Any keyword hit?}
    D -->|yes| E[Use keyword emotion]
    D -->|no| F[Use neutral]

    B -->|Legacy voice| G[Audio emotion classifier]
    G --> H[Keyword emotion detector]
    H --> I{Text score is 0?}
    I -->|yes| J{Audio score is 0?}
    J -->|yes| F
    J -->|no| K[Use audio emotion]
    I -->|no| L{Audio score < 0.55?}
    L -->|yes| E
    L -->|no| M{Audio neutral/calm and text score >= 0.45?}
    M -->|yes| E
    M -->|no| N{Text score >= audio score + 0.12?}
    N -->|yes| E
    N -->|no| K

    B -->|SenseVoice optional| O[SenseVoice tag extraction]
    O --> P[Map tags to emotion]
```

## Prompt Context Sent To The LLM

The LLM receives the rendered `prompts/jarvis_chat.txt` template. The context payload
contains:

- `detected_emotion`
- `emotion_guidance`
- `user_profile`
- recent `conversation_history`
- optional `wellness_signal`

The prompt instructs Jarvis to be calm, concise, practical, easy to say out loud,
emotion-aware, supportive during distress, and careful not to invent personal facts.

## API Surface So Far

| Endpoint | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /` | Basic service status message |
| `GET /ui` | Browser voice console |
| `GET /health` | Provider status for LLM, STT, emotion, TTS, and database |
| `POST /api/chat` | Text chat turn |
| `POST /api/voice` | Voice upload turn with optional transcript override and wellness inputs |
| `GET /api/personas` | List available persona profiles |
| `GET /api/history/{session_id}` | Fetch recent conversation turns |
| `DELETE /api/history/{session_id}` | Clear a session's conversation history |
| `WS /ws/chat` | Minimal websocket chat path using neutral emotion and no memory |

## Project Status So Far

- Working backend app factory and FastAPI routes are in place.
- Browser UI supports text, voice recording, wake phrase listening, playback speed,
  emotion display, raw JSON diagnostics, and history.
- Bedrock is the current LLM provider in `.env`.
- Legacy voice mode is active: Whisper plus hybrid emotion detection.
- SenseVoice is implemented but currently disabled by configuration.
- TTS attempts Coqui synthesis and gracefully falls back to text output when Coqui is
  unavailable.
- Conversation history is persisted per session and cleared on app startup.
